facts.statement: Ludwig Döderlein first named and described Anurognathus in 1923.
facts.quote: Anurognathus was first named and described by Ludwig Döderlein in 1923.

facts.statement: The species name ammoni honors the Bavarian geologist Ludwig von Ammon, whose collection provided the fossil Döderlein acquired in 1922.
facts.quote: The specific name ammoni honours the Bavarian geologist Ludwig von Ammon, from whose collection Döderlein had acquired the fossil in 1922.

facts.statement: Anurognathus had a short head equipped with pin-like teeth adapted for catching insects.
facts.quote: Anurognathus had a short head with pin-like teeth for catching insects.

facts.statement: Despite being traditionally grouped with long-tailed pterosaurs, Anurognathus possessed a comparatively short tail that enhanced its maneuverability for hunting.
facts.quote: Although it traditionally is ascribed to the long-tailed pterosaur group "Rhamphorhynchoidea", its tail was comparatively short, allowing it more maneuverability for hunting.

facts.statement: Mark P. Witton estimated the mass of a 35 cm wingspan specimen of Anurognathus to be 40 grams in 2008.
facts.quote: In 2008, Mark P. Witton estimated a mass of 40 g for a specimen with a 35 cm wingspan.

facts.statement: Studies revealed that the skull of Anurognathus was very short and broad, being wider than it was long.
facts.quote: The skull was shown to have been very short and broad, wider than long.

facts.statement: Anurognathus likely possessed very large eyes supported by enormous orbits, providing high visual acuity in dim light and some binocular vision due to forward-pointing eyes.
facts.quote: The proportionally enormous orbits of Anurognathus most likely supported very large eyes, which may have given Anurognathus high visual acuity in dim light conditions, its eyes also pointed forward to a degree, providing some binocular vision.

facts.statement: Researcher S. Christopher Bennett interpreted bumps on the holotype jaws as evidence of a protruding bristle formed by hairs on the snout.
facts.quote: Bennett also restudied the holotype, interpreting bumps on the jaws as an indication that hairs forming a protruding bristle were present on the snout.

facts.statement: Evidence of a membrane near the shin indicated that Anurognathus's wing contacted the ankle, resulting in a short and broad wing shape.
facts.quote: A membrane, visible near the shin, showed that the wing contacted the ankle and was thus rather short and broad.

facts.statement: Anurognathus lived approximately 150 million years ago during the Late Jurassic (Tithonian) in Europe, specifically in the Altmühltal Formation of Germany.
facts.quote: Anurognathus es un género extinto de pterosaurio ranforrincoideo que vivió hace aproximadamente 150 millones de años a finales del período Jurásico (Titoniense) en Europa, específicamente de la Formación Altmühltal en Alemania.

facts.statement: S. Christopher Bennett inferred that Anurognathus was a slower-flying predator specialized in maneuverability, with large eyes adapted for a crepuscular lifestyle.
facts.quote: Bennett, however, infers from the discovery of the true shorter size of the wings, combined with the short tail, that it was a slower flying predator, specialised in hunting by maneuverability, its large eyes adapted to a crepuscular way of life.

facts.statement: Research predicting a gape of 1734 mm² for Anurognathus concluded that its prey would have been very small, around 11 mm in length.
facts.quote: They predicted 1734 mm2 for the estimated gaps provided from the holotype of Anurognathus, Dendrorhynchoides, and Jeholopterus. The research team ended up concluding that consumed prey would have to be very small in length, around 11 mm total.

facts.statement: Oskar Kuhn assigned Anurognathus to the family Anurognathidae in 1937.
facts.quote: Anurognathus was assigned by Oskar Kuhn to the family Anurognathidae in 1937.

facts.statement: A 2021 phylogenetic analysis by Xuefang Wei and colleagues placed Anurognathus within the subfamily Anurognathinae of the family Anurognathidae.
facts.quote: In 2021, a phylogenetic analysis conducted by Xuefang Wei and colleagues recovered Anurognathus within the subfamily Anurognathinae, a subfamily within the family Anurognathidae.

facts.statement: Ludwig Döderlein originally suggested that Anurognathus was a swift flyer similar to a modern nightjar, a view later challenged by findings of shorter wings.
facts.quote: According to Döderlein Anurognathus was, with its long wings, a swift flyer, surprising its prey, similar to the modern nightjar.

facts.statement: Peter Wellnhofer redescribed the holotype of Anurognathus in 1975.
facts.quote: The holotype was redescribed by Peter Wellnhofer in 1975.

facts.statement: A second, smaller specimen found later provided new anatomical information, confirming the skull was very short and broad.
facts.quote: It provided new information on many points of the anatomy. The skull was shown to have been very short and broad, wider than long.

facts.statement: Peter Wellnhofer incorrectly reconstructed the skull in 1975 by mistaking large eye sockets for antorbital fenestrae, whereas in Anurognathus these openings are small and located at the front of the snout.
facts.quote: It transpired that Wellnhofer had incorrectly reconstructed the skull in 1975, mistaking the large eye sockets for the fenestrae antorbitales, skull openings that in most pterosaurs are larger than the orbits but in Anurognathus they are small and together with the nostrils are placed at the front of the flat snout.

facts.statement: Most of the Anurognathus skull consisted of bone struts.
facts.quote: Most of the skull consisted of bone struts.

facts.statement: Investigation showed that Anurognathus lacked a pygostyle and possessed nine unfused but very reduced tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The presumed pygostyle was absent; investigating the real nine tail vertebrae instead of impressions showed that they were unfused, though very reduced.

facts.statement: The wing finger of Anurognathus lacked the fourth phalanx.
facts.quote: The wing finger lacked the fourth phalanx.

facts.statement: The genus Anurognathus is based on the holotype BSP 1922.I.42, found in the Solnhofen Limestone near Eichstätt.
facts.quote: El género está basado en el holotipo BSP 1922.I.42 (Bayerische Staatssammlung für Palaeontologie und Geologie), hallado en la Caliza de Solnhofen cerca de Eichstätt.

facts.statement: Anurognathus had a short head with needle-like teeth used to catch insects.
facts.quote: Anurognathus tenía una cabeza corta con dientes semejantes a agujas para atrapar insectos

facts.statement: Although traditionally assigned to the long-tailed pterosaur group Rhamphorhynchoidea, Anurognathus had a comparatively short tail.
facts.quote: aunque tradicionalmente se ha adscrito al grupo de pterosaurios de cola larga "Rhamphorhynchoidea", su cola era comparativamente corta

facts.statement: Anurognathus had an estimated wingspan of fifty centimeters and a body length of nine centimeters including the skull.
facts.quote: Con una envergadura estimada de cincuenta centímetros y una longitud corporal (cráneo incluido) de nueve centímetros

facts.statement: In 2008, Mark Paul Witton estimated a mass of forty grams for a specimen with a wingspan of thirty-five centimeters.
facts.quote: en 2008 Mark Paul Witton estimó una masa de cuarenta gramos para un espécimen con una envergadura de 35 centímetros

facts.statement: The holotype was redescribed by Peter Wellnhofer in 1975.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue redescrito por Peter Wellnhofer en 1975.

facts.statement: A second, smaller specimen, likely a subadult, was found later; its plates were sold to private collections without official records and were described by S. Christopher Bennet in 2007.
facts.quote: Más tarde se halló un segundo espécimen más pequeño, probablemente de un individuo subadulto. Su lámina y contralámina estaban separadas y ambas fueron vendidas a colecciones privadas; ninguna tiene un registro oficial. Fueron descritas por S. Christopher Bennet en 2007.

facts.statement: The plates show impressions of most of the flight membrane, and under ultraviolet light, remains of thigh and arm muscles are visible.
facts.quote: Las láminas muestran impresiones de una gran parte de la membrana de vuelo y bajo la luz ultravioleta son visibles restos de los músculos del muslo y del brazo.

facts.statement: This indicates that Wellnhofer incorrectly reconstructed the skull in 1975 by confusing the large eye sockets with the antorbital fenestrae.
facts.quote: Esto indica que Wellnhofer había reconstruido incorrectamente el cráneo en 1975, confundiendo las grandes cuencas oculares con las fenestras antorbitales

facts.statement: The eyes pointed forward to some degree, giving it some binocular vision.
facts.quote: Los ojos apuntaban hacia adelante en cierto grado, dándole alguna visión binocular.

facts.statement: The presumed pygostyle was absent; investigation of the actual vertebrae showed it had nine unfused, though very reduced, vertebrae.
facts.quote: El presunto pigóstilo estaba ausente; la investigación de las vértebras reales en vez de la impresión mostró que en realidad tenía nueve vértebras sin fusionar, aunque muy reducidas.

facts.statement: According to Bennet, a membrane visible near the shin shows the wing connected to the ankle, meaning they were short and broad.
facts.quote: Según Bennet, una membrana, visible cerca de la espinilla, muestra que el ala se conectaba al tobillo y por lo tanto eran cortas y anchas.

facts.statement: Bennett also redescribed the holotype, interpreting bumps on its jaws as evidence of bristles present on the snout.
facts.quote: Bennett también reestudió el holotipo, interpretando las protuberancias en sus mandíbulas como una indicación de que tenía pelos que formaban unas cerdas sobresalientes presentes sobre el hocico.

facts.statement: Anurognathus was assigned to the family Anurognathidae by Oskar Kuhn in 1937.
facts.quote: Anurognathus fue asignado en 1937 por Oskar Kuhn a la familia Anurognathidae.

facts.statement: In the current clade Anurognathidae, Anurognathus is the sister taxon to the clade Asiaticognathidae, which contains the genera Batrachognathus, Dendrorhynchoides, and Jeholopterus.
facts.quote: En el actual clado Anurognathidae, Anurognathus es el taxón hermano del clado Asiaticognathidae, el cual contiene los géneros Batrachognathus, Dendrorhynchoides y Jeholopterus.

facts.statement: According to Döderlein, Anurognathus was a fast flyer that surprised its prey with its long wings, similar to the modern swift.
facts.quote: Según Döderlein Anurognathus era, con sus largas alas, un rápido volador que sorprendía a sus presas, de forma similar al actual chotacabras.

facts.statement: However, Bennet inferred from the discovery of the true short wing size combined with the short tail that it was a slow-flying predator specialized in hunting with maneuverability, with large eyes adapted to a crepuscular lifestyle.
facts.quote: Sin embargo Bennett infirió del descubrimiento del verdadero tamaño corto de las alas, combinado con la cola corta, que era un depredador volador lento, especializado en cazar con su maniobrabilidad, con grandes ojos adaptados a una forma de vida crepuscular.

facts.statement: The genus name Anurognathus was established by Döderlein in 1923.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Anurognathus (genus), Döderlein 1923

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Anurognathus ammoni.
facts.quote: Type species: Anurognathus ammoni

facts.statement: Anurognathus lived during the Tithonian stage, from 149.2 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: According to Döderlein, the reduced tail of Anurognathus was similar to the pygostyle of modern birds.
facts.quote: Según Döderlein la cola reducida de Anurognathus era similar al pigóstilo de las aves modernas.

facts.statement: Typical rhamphorhynchoid traits of Anurognathus include an elongated fifth toe and short neck and metacarpals.
facts.quote: Sus rasgos de "ranforrincoide" típico incluyen su quinto dedo del pie alargado y cuello y metacarpos cortos.

facts.statement: The wing finger lacked the fourth phalanx.
facts.quote: El dedo del ala carecía de la cuarta falange.

facts.statement: Anurognathus was featured in the second episode of the BBC documentary Walking with Dinosaurs, appearing in a mutual symbiotic relationship with the dinosaur Diplodocus, eating parasites from its skin.
facts.quote: Anurognathus fue representado en el segundo episodio de la miniserie documental de la BBC Walking with Dinosaurs, en la cual aparece en una relación simbiótica mutua con el dinosaurio Diplodocus, comiendo insectos parásito de su piel.

facts.statement: Anurognathus appeared in the fifth episode of the ITV sci-fi series Primeval, where it was incorrectly depicted living in the Late Cretaceous, 85 million years ago, with piranha-like behavior.
facts.quote: Anurognathus apareció en el quinto episodio de la serie de televisión de ciencia ficción de ITV Primeval. Aquí, Anurognathus fue representado erróneamente viviendo en el período Cretácico Superior, hace 85 millones de años, con un comportamiento parecido al de una piraña.

facts.statement: A flock was shown devouring the flesh of a carcass in minutes, a strange behavior considering anatomical evidence shows this species was an insectivore more similar to modern podargos.
facts.quote: Se mostró a una parvada devorando la carne de un cadáver en cuestión de minutos, un comportamiento extraño teniendo en cuenta que la evidencia anatómica muestra que esta especie era un insectívoro más similar a los modernos podargos.

rejected.quote: Anurognathus (from the Greek ανουρα γναθος "frog jaw") is an extinct genus of small pterosaur from the Late Jurassic Altmühltal Formation of Germany.
